Stated: 'PBPK model for PF-05089771 predicted a 1 g oral dose would be required to achieve exposures of approximately 12x Nav1.7 IC50 at Cmax'; 'In a subsequent single ascending oral dose clinical study, the predictions for PF-05089771 compared well with observed data.' Healthy-volunteer PK counts: dose same, comparison_stated true, 2016. This model, not iPSC neurons, set the IEM dose (1600 mg). Whether Cao 2016 reports IEM-patient exposure vs the IC50 multiple was not checked (paywalled).

Possible dose/engagement context: Siebenga et al. 2020 (Clin Transl Sci, PMC7070789) healthy-volunteer evoked-pain battery found no PF-05089771 analgesia. It is a human readout, not a model compared with patients, so likely no new track; listed for the drafter to rule out.
rule_questions: Patient-level genotype-to-drug-response predictions in IEM (structural modelling plus iPSC/DRG functional profiling predicting carbamazepine response of Nav1.7-V400M/S241T; Yang 2012 Nat Commun, Geha 2016 JAMA Neurol) use a non-selective drug outside the member list. Under the class rule they do not score, but the brief does not say whether a patient-level model validated only on a non-member drug should be listed as an untested track for the class.

Funapide (XEN402) is described in some sources as a broader Nav blocker (Nav1.7 plus other subtypes). The tile lists it as a member; checker accepted the given class table without re-deciding selectivity.

A drug-independent model (SCN9A genetics, 2006) opening a track for a later member drug/route: rule 6 says open at model_first_use_year, but efficacy 4 and 6 open at the drug's first IEM trial start (2011, 2012). Which year should a per-drug opener carry?
